beliefs_note: Priors are the author's, written before any check ran, and are Zach's to overwrite. Verdicts follow the RET ledger: CONFIRMED, FALSIFIED, REVISED, OPEN. `scope` and `frame` come from the lists `scopes` and `frames`, fixed before any belief resolves. A resolved belief needs `resolved_on`, and `reason_logged_at` must not be later than it. `pr` (optional) is the probability of REVISED, which turns the score into a three-outcome score.

Comfortable slack everywhere is a warning sign, not a result; check what was left out
lessons.gate: inlier (--strict fails when min slack is over half the window)

base_case.rule: Pinned. It equals the earliest anchor on file (2026-05-04) + 12 months - 30 day buffer. Other anchors are scenarios. If any anchor would put the date earlier than this, the base_case gate fails and the plan must be re-based on purpose.

sim.note: Duration spreads are author estimates (multipliers on each step's days: optimistic, likely, pessimistic), not measurements. A step may set dur {opt, likely, pess} or measured true. Durations are sampled as floats and steps fire when their preconditions finish (event time); the 12-month window is the only hard calendar edge, plus any step window.not_before.

stall.note: Author priors for heavy-tailed stalls: with probability p a step suffers an extra exponential delay with mean mean_mult times its likely duration. The repo merge gaps show a long tail (median about 5 minutes, p99 about 22 hours, burstiness 0.64) but there are no step-duration data for people or counsel, so these numbers are not measurements.

types.instant: a sampled finish time, reported as an interval (percentiles), never a point
types.order: the needs edges: a partial order of what must finish before what
types.duration: a distribution (triangular), sampled as a float number of days
types.branch: a path patch over the graph; branches are compared under common random numbers and are not weighted by the author

paths.title: Sequential (baseline)
paths.summary: Verify the ledger, hand it to counsel, tier the mechanisms, draft, review, file.
tradeoffs: One filing and one one-way door before the date
Counsel starts only after the ledger is verified, so it uses the most calendar time
Lowest rework risk: claims rest on verified facts

paths.title: Thin provisional early, full ledger in parallel
paths.summary: File a thin provisional on the mechanisms with no known public trace as soon as counsel is engaged; finish the ledger and the full filing afterwards.

nodes_add.title: Pick the mechanisms with no known public trace so far; counsel confirms the cut
Draft a thin provisional on that subset
Write-lock declaration: thin filing
nodes_add.declare: Filing a thin provisional is a one-way door: the subset and the date are fixed. Declare only when the cut of mechanisms is confirmed by counsel.

tradeoffs: Two filings and two one-way doors, so more counsel cost
Only the confirmed subset is covered by the date; already-disclosed mechanisms wait for the full filing
Depends on the cut being right: a mechanism wrongly judged never-public would be filed on weaker facts
Counsel decides whether a later filing can build on the thin one

paths.title: Draft in parallel with the ledger
paths.summary: Counsel and the inventory start now; the ledger is only required before review.
tradeoffs: Shortest critical path of the three
Counsel receives facts that are still marked UNVERIFIED, so drafts may need rework if the audit log or the prior-filings answer changes the picture
One filing and one one-way door, same as sequential

sim_findings.note: The date itself is safe on the author's numbers (about 97 to 100 percent) but the margin is mostly cushion in the date: if the real deadline were 90 days earlier the chance falls to 76 percent bounded and 47 percent with stalls, and at 120 days earlier it is about 0. The plan's real risk is a wrong anchor, not slow work.
